supersedes: v1 (commit 296f331, sha256 bf81026143d0cb8415667509e1d650b0b7efad7de24eb7907ea4002054bf9491), reissued after bridge run B1 (docs/specs/pala-1/independent-runs/turak/scitt-statement/): F1 - kid added to the protected header (RFC 9943 section 6 MUST absent x5t/x5chain); F2 - content type declared in the protected header; F4 - the CWT subject now carries the FULL chain head (the 16-hex truncation collided across chains at a 64-bit birthday bound); F3 - the sha256/length fields below are rescoped, see expected.note.
purpose: A deterministic COSE_Sign1 Signed Statement over the published PALA-1 core-vector chain head, reproducible byte-for-byte from public standards alone. Real crypto, fake entropy - never use this key outside a test vector.

key.source: RFC 8032, section 7.1, TEST 1 - a published test key, chosen so nothing about it is ours

statement_inputs.subject: pala-1:chain:3a1a3673f50498eb1d1c6f94b983d6c606cd85ed53627b4e4ffe55153c7af813
statement_inputs.subject_note: the FULL 32-byte head in hex - a truncated subject collides across chains at the truncation's birthday bound, and a transparency service indexes by this value (B1 finding F4)
statement_inputs.kid_note: protected header label 4 = RFC 9679 COSE Key Thumbprint (SHA-256) of the verification key; in the PROTECTED bucket because an unprotected kid is unauthenticated (B1 adversarial case A10)
statement_inputs.content_type_note: protected header label 3; names the payload schema so it is never read as a CWT Claims Set (B1 finding F2, ambiguity A8). Vendor tree, unregistered.
statement_inputs.cwt_claims_note: issuer -> CWT claim key 1, subject -> CWT claim key 2, carried in the COSE protected header under label 15 (RFC 9597)
statement_inputs.payload_note: attached CBOR map: {1: chain head (32 bytes), 2: first_seq, 3: last_seq, 4: 'pala-1/v1.0'}
statement_inputs.protected_header_order_note: labels appear in ascending order (1, 3, 4, 15) - RFC 8949 section 4.2.1 deterministic form; a strict decoder accepts without reordering

byte_stability.note: Four ways 'the same statement' can honestly differ in bytes. 'The signature verifies' and 'these are the published bytes' are two different claims; check the one you mean.
byte_stability.1_signature_determinism: Byte-for-byte reproduction is claimable here ONLY because the alg is EdDSA - RFC 8032 makes the signature deterministic by construction, confirmed across three runs in B1. ES256 has no such guarantee from the standard: RFC 6979 derandomisation is a per-library choice (a common COSE stack applies it; a common raw-ECDSA stack does not), so two conforming implementations legitimately emit different signature bytes over identical input. An ES256 vector could claim 'verifies', never 'reproduces'.
byte_stability.2_unprotected_bucket: The unprotected map is outside the Sig_structure. Content placed or moved there changes the artifact's bytes while the signature keeps verifying (measured: moving kid to unprotected grew a test statement and left verification green). This statement carries an EMPTY unprotected map; every meaningful parameter is protected.
byte_stability.3_tag_18: This statement is the TAGGED COSE_Sign1 form - first byte 0xd2 (CBOR tag 18). Libraries disagree on emitting/requiring the tag; an untagged re-encoding (starting 0x84) of the same content is a different artifact. A byte comparison must reject or explicitly normalise it.
byte_stability.4_sig_structure: What is signed is not the message but the separately assembled CBOR array ["Signature1", protected, external_aad, payload] (RFC 9052 section 4.4). Two implementations must build those bytes identically - deterministic CBOR again - or signatures over identical inputs will not agree.

expected.note: statement_sha256 and statement_length_bytes are expectations for THIS deterministic encoder emitting the TAGGED form - not signature-bound identities. COSE malleability outside the Sig_structure (B1 finding F3, adversarial case A1: re-encoding a CBOR length head keeps the signature valid and changes both fields) means artifact identity and signature validity must be checked separately.

tamper_expectations: flip any bit of the 32-byte head inside the payload: signature verification MUST fail (the payload is signed)
flip any bit of the signature: verification MUST fail
verify against a different expected head: the commitment check MUST fail even though the signature is valid
move kid from the protected to the unprotected map: the signature still verifies AND the bytes are no longer the published statement - the two checks are distinct (byte_stability mode 2; B1 case A10)
strip the outer tag 18 (0xd2): the content is unchanged but the artifact differs in its first byte; a byte-exact consumer MUST treat it as a different statement (byte_stability mode 3)
